reviewProfile: UX implementation, browser assertions and visual inspection
scope: Versioned HTTP tests of the owning Story DEV deployment. Every new browser scenario intercepts HTTP. Synthetic cases, writes, results and Task status remain isolated test fixtures; no operational application, business record or agent result changes.

navigation.entry: Story or current Task > Execution > DEV > Test version
navigation.ordering: Build, publication, then tests. No new navigation tab or visual identity. Technical references and per-case HTTP details remain collapsed.
navigation.recovery: One test controller per owning Story, mounted across tabs. Lost acknowledgment preserves exact body/persona/key and reason across reload. External recovery returns to the same result after the journey central focus has settled.
navigation.correction: Request correction reveals/focuses the existing development-cycle decision and Gateway of Specification flow. It does not send a test, code-generation or status command.

behaviorReviewed: The preview enumerates all cases of the fixed suite, with source/deployment/suite references, names, methods, paths, expected status and one-based G1 criterion references. Complete acceptance coverage is separate from technical verification.

For mutatesData, a visible warning identifies the marked concrete write cases by name/method/path and the checkbox authorizes those effects. Payload stays in the controlled build source; no payload preview or arbitrary target is claimed.

Technical success does not approve business criteria or finish the Test Task. Acceptance refers to its fixed suite/revision; only the backend may complete the Test Task. The UI links to the recorded Task and refreshes its journey after terminal results.
A failed operation with case results is a test rejection. A failed executor with no cases is distinguished explicitly and does not invent rejected acceptance criteria.

Historical evidence uses the names/criterion indices preserved with that suite. A later context never renames an earlier result. Current scope requires the server current flag, fresh reading and healthy observation naming the same deployment.

Old commit, another active deployment, unavailable target or reading failure preserve dated evidence while removing the assertion of current coverage. These tests never approve Development Finished or complete a Story.

Real Admin/Product Owner/Architect role, current Story/Task context, reason, explicit checkbox and a confirmed preview govern new decisions. Foreign/malformed context and incomplete G1 acceptance remain blocked.

Original acknowledgment replay and unknown-result reconciliation reuse the existing operation; resume and pre-dispatch cancellation require distinct confirmations and do not undo earlier data effects.
Thirteen DEVELOPMENT_TEST action labels and development_test target are translated without conflating Task status, operational state, test outcome or Story completion.

tests.qualification: The complete selected set was rerun after fixes; repeated executions are not counted as new cases. Browser fixtures simulate every provider and do not attest real HTTP execution.
tests.initialFindings: Two assertions searched for DONE while the retained tasks.q filter excluded the Task; the corrected scenario clears that filter through the interface. Two failures found real focus contention between the recovery result and journey central section; return focus now waits for the latter. Preliminary rejection captures were at page top; final captures scroll the relevant preview/evidence into view below the established sticky rail.

assertions: Confirmation/result/return focus and focused correction entry
Explicit labeled reason/checkbox, disabled roles and incomplete coverage
No document horizontal overflow in preview
Original request identity preserved across tabs/persona/reload
accessibility.visual: Six final viewport captures inspected for shell/rail context, wrapping, clear case names/results, concrete data-write notice, blue primary and disabled controls.
limits: No comprehensive screen-reader, WCAG, keyboard-only or cross-browser certification is claimed.
Viewport captures show the visible portion of a long DEV flow, not every control/reference at once.
Current Story lifecycle summaries in the synthetic fixture remain explicitly unconfirmed rather than fabricated production evidence.

metrics: Existing indicators retained; no new indicator or target.
outsideScope: API/shared/runtime implementations and real HTTP acceptance, owned by the parent receipt
Arbitrary test scripts, free-form endpoints, payload/secret projection
Automatic code correction or G1 approval
Release candidates, QA/HML/PRD promotion or Story completion
